newsitem.title: USA: Bill proposed after rape of comatose woman.
newsitem.headline: Bill proposed after rape of comatose woman.

text.p: Following the case of a nursing home aide who raped and impregnated a comatose patient, legislation was introduced in New York state Tuesday to allow criminal checks of health workers and impose stiff prison sentences for those who abuse patients.

The bill, designed to protect patients in the state's 660 nursing homes, would create a new felony-level crime of patient abuse, with penalties of as much as seven years in prison for a first offence, authorities said.
The legislation was dubbed "Kathy's Law" after a 30-year-old woman who was raped at the Westfall Health Care Centre in Brighton, New York, near Rochester.
Nursing home aide John Horace was convicted last week of rape and sexual assault of the woman, whose full name has not been disclosed, and is to be sentenced at the end of the month.
She gave birth to a boy last March 18. The baby, who is being raised by his maternal grandmother, has a congenital heart condition and underwent surgery last week in an effort to correct the problem.
"Kathy's family is thrilled to lend her name to this worthwhile legislation," said her mother, whose identity also has been withheld from the public.
The measure also would require nursing home and home health care applicants to reveal any criminal convictions and sign sworn statements.

Horace faces up to 25 years in prison. He was convicted of raping the woman during a five-week job he held at the nursing home in August 1995. Horace also has been convicted of fondling another Westfall patient, a 49-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis.
His rape victim has been in a coma since a car accident 11 years ago when she was a freshman at Cornell University in Ithaca, N.Y.
